Sample Size or Power Calculation for Two-Sample Mean Test

Source: R/two_mean_size.R
two_mean_size.Rd

Calculates the required sample size or achieved power for testing the difference between two independent population means. Supports two-sided, one-sided, non-inferiority, and equivalence tests.

Usage

two_mean_size(
  muA,
  muB,
  delta = NULL,
  kappa = 1,
  sd = NULL,
  sdA = NULL,
  sdB = NULL,
  alpha,
  beta = NULL,
  nA = NULL,
  nB = NULL,
  test_type = "2-side"
)

Arguments

muA

Numeric. Mean of group A

muB

Numeric. Mean of group B

delta

Numeric (optional). Margin for non-inferiority or equivalence tests. Required for "non-inferiority" and "equivalence" tests.

kappa

Numeric. Sample size ratio (nA / nB). Defaults to 1.

sd

Numeric (optional). Standard deviation. Required for "2-side", "non-inferiority", and "equivalence" tests.

sdA

Numeric (optional). Standard deviation of group A. Required for "1-side" tests.

sdB

Numeric (optional). Standard deviation of group B. Required for "1-side" tests.

alpha

Numeric. Type I error rate.

beta

Numeric (optional). Type II error rate (1 - power). Required for sample size calculation.

nA

Integer (optional). Sample size of group A. Required when calculating power for "1-side" tests.

nB

Integer (optional). Sample size of group B. Required when calculating power for "2-side", "non-inferiority", and "equivalence" tests.

test_type

Character. Type of test: "2-side", "1-side", "non-inferiority", or "equivalence".

Value

Numeric. Returns the required sample size (if beta is given), or the power (if n* is given).

Note

Only one of beta or n* should be specified. Supplying both will result in undefined behavior. For "2-side", "non-inferiority", and "equivalence" tests, sd is required. When calculating power for "2-side", "non-inferiority", and "equivalence" tests, nB is required. For "1-side" tests, sdA, sdB are required. When calculating power for "1-side" tests, nA is required.

Examples

# Required sample size for two-sided test
two_mean_size(muA = 5, muB = 10, kappa = 1, sd = 10, alpha = 0.05, beta = 0.2, test_type = "2-side")
#> [1] 63

# Power of two-sided test
two_mean_size(muA = 5, muB = 10, kappa = 1, sd = 10, alpha = 0.05, nB = 63, test_type = "2-side")
#> [1] 0.8013024

# Required sample size for one-sided test
two_mean_size(muA = 132.86, muB = 127.44, kappa = 2, sdA = 15.34, sdB = 18.23, alpha = 0.05, beta = 0.2, test_type = "1-side")
#> [1] 85

# Power of one-sided test
two_mean_size(muA = 132.86, muB = 127.44, kappa = 2, sdA = 15.34, sdB = 18.23, alpha = 0.05, nA = 85, test_type = "1-side")
#> [1] 0.8020669

# Required sample size for non-inferiority test
two_mean_size(muA = 5, muB = 5, delta = 5, kappa = 1, sd = 10, alpha = 0.05, beta = 0.2, test_type = "non-inferiority")
#> [1] 50

# Power of non-inferiority test
two_mean_size(muA = 5, muB = 5, delta = 5, kappa = 1, sd = 10, alpha = 0.05, nB = 50, test_type = "non-inferiority")
#> [1] 0.8037819

# Required sample size for equivalence test
two_mean_size(muA = 5, muB = 4, delta = 5, kappa = 1, sd = 10, alpha = 0.05, beta = 0.2, test_type = "equivalence")
#> [1] 108

# Power of equivalence test
two_mean_size(muA = 5, muB = 4, delta = 5, kappa = 1, sd = 10, alpha = 0.05, nB = 108, test_type = "equivalence")
#> [1] 0.8045235
